newsitem.title: BURMA: Jailed Burmese opposition party member dies. [Corrected 08:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Jailed Burmese opposition party member dies. [Corrected 08:55 GMT]

text.p: A jailed opposition party member died of heart disease in Burma on Sunday, a government statement said. (Corrects status of deceased politician from MP to member of the opposition party).

Tin Shwe, 67, from northern Mandalay, was jailed in 1991 on charges of instigating civil unrest and attempting to form a parallel government to the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC), said the statement, which was released on Monday.
He died at Rangoon general hospital.

Tin Shwe was among scores of members of Burmese opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy Party (NLD) who were arrested after the party's landslide election victory in May 1990, which the SLORC never recognised.
The SLORC has kept a tight rein on the NLD ever since the election and thwarted attempts by the party to hold special gatherings or to conduct political activities.

Last month, the NLD said that 316 of its members had been held by the SLORC to prevent them attending a special gathering at Suu Kyi's home to mark the seventh anniversary of the party's election win.
The detained politicians were later released, it said.
